chunks: And from his sermon (peace be upon him) in warning the people of Nahrawan

He will take you out from a prayer you used to pray to a prayer you did not used to pray. When Friday night comes, a leader will rise among you with the sword, striking the head of one of you, shedding his blood, removing his turban, and placing it between his eyes. Then he will kill your companion and carry his head to a king of the kings of the earth, saying: 'This is the head of so-and-so, and this is the head of so-and-so, and this is the head of so-and-so,' until he takes them out of their religion, and takes them out of their land, and takes them out of their home, and takes them out of their wealth, and takes them out of their children, and takes them out of their souls, and takes them out of their bodies, and takes them out of their likenesses, and takes them out of their types, and takes them out of their colors, and takes them out of their descriptions, and takes them out of their opposites, and takes them out of their difference, and takes them out of their difference from others, and takes them out of their difference from the difference of others, until God alone is He, with no partner, and the religion is for God alone, with no partner.
ai.seo_question: What is the fate of the Khawarij according to Imam Ali's sermon in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) delivers this prophetic sermon to the Khawarij of Nahrawan, foretelling the rise of a leader who will kill one of their own and carry his head to a king, leading to their expulsion from religion, land, wealth, and families. This event is historically identified as the killing of Abdullah ibn al-Hanafiyya by the Khawarij, with his head presented to Caliph Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan, fulfilling the Imam's warning. The sermon emphasizes their deviation from true Islam, leaving God alone with no partner, as they were the first to declare takfir against the Commander of the Faithful.
